The number of ‘poles’ of a filter affects the filter's rolloff, how sharply the filter cuts off. In technical terms, each pole of the filter attenuates (reduces the volume of) frequencies beyond the filter point by 6db per octave.

More Poles = Sharper Filter Cutoff

Lomparative filtering effects of the four low pass filters Adding RESONANCE bocste the armplitude at the ntial cutoff pont.

A one pole low pass filter will attenuate frequencies by 6db per octave beyond the filter point; 12db two octaves beyond. 18db three octaves beyond. etc. A two pole filter attenuates at 12db per octave, a three pole at 18db per octave, and a four pole filter at 24db per octave. In musical terms, fewer filter poles results in a brighter, buzzier sound; while more poles makes for a fatter sound.

VCAs The VCF ; VCA page also contains the two output VCAs that are used to control the volume of the sound. VCASs act just like the volume control on your stereo: you turn it up it gets louder, you turn it down it gets softer.

VCASs have generally been “invisible” on programmable synthesizers, controlled only by the volume envelope generator. The Xpander has 15 VCAs strategically located throughout each voice because they are usetul tools. The two VCAs in the VCF ; VCA page are the ones through which the synthesizer's sound passes, and are therefore most important. itis from these VCASs that enveloping of the entire sound occurs. In working with these VCAS remem- ber that no sound will come out of the voice unless both VCASs are turned up, either by the gain of the VCA itself or by modulating the VCA. with an envelope. LFO. or some other source. Velocity is useful as a modulator for one of the VCAs, because the harder you play the keyboard. the higher the output volume will be.

It the initial amplitude of both VCAS are up. the sound ot the voice will always be heard. even when no notes are being played.
